C: SOQL is for querying standard Salesforce CRM objects (Accounts, Contacts), not Data 360 DMOs. D: JSON is a data interchange format, not a query language for retrieving records from DMOs.

question: A hotel booking platform wants to identify users who have searched for the same city more than three times within a 10-minute window. These users should be instantly added to a "High Intent" segment and receive a push notification. Which Data 360 feature should process this real-time pattern

options.A: A streaming insight with a sliding window count aggregation
options.B: A calculated insight refreshed every 10 minutes
options.C: A batch transform scheduled every 5 minutes
options.D: A streaming data transform that processes each event individually

explanation: A streaming insight continuously processes event streams and can detect patterns like "more than three searches within 10 minutes" using windowed aggregations (sliding or tumbling windows). Results are immediately available for segmentation and can trigger data actions, meeting the near-real-time requirement. Why the other options are incorrect: B: A calculated insight refreshed every 10 minutes cannot detect a rolling 10-minute window in real time; it would have up to 10 minutes of latency. C: A batch transform scheduled every 5 minutes still introduces latency (up to 5 minutes) and cannot maintain a true rolling 10-minute window. D: A streaming data transform processes individual events but does not perform windowed aggregations like counting over a time window.

question: A technical support director wants to deploy a generative AI chatbot to help customers troubleshoot product issues. They are concerned the AI will give generic or incorrect answers without access to the company's internal product manuals, troubleshooting guides, and known issue databases. Which Data 360 feature ensures the AI uses this internal content to generate accurate, context-specific responses

options.A: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to inject relevant internal documents into the AI prompt
options.B: Vector embedding compression to reduce the size of internal knowledge bases
options.C: Automated conversion of all internal documents to Salesforce Knowledge articles
options.D: Generative fine-tuning of the base model on internal support transcripts

explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds AI prompts with relevant internal data from Data 360. RAG retrieves contextually relevant information from product manuals, troubleshooting guides, and known issue databases, then augments the prompt to the LLM. This ensures the AI generates accurate, contextually relevant responses based on internal data. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Vector embedding compression is an optimization technique but does not itself retrieve or ground AI responses; it only reduces storage/compute. C: Converting documents to Knowledge articles is helpful but does not automatically enable RAG-based contextual retrieval; you still need a retrieval mechanism.

question: A financial services firm wants its external analytics team working in Google BigQuery to query unified customer profiles stored in Data 360. The solution must provide read-only access with minimal latency and no data duplication. Which capability should the consultant use to expose Data 360 objects to BigQuery

options.A: Data 360 Data Shares with zero-copy sharing
options.B: Scheduled batch exports from Data 360 to Cloud Storage
options.C: REST API endpoints with paginated customer data
options.D: Custom ODBC connector configured for cross-platform queries

explanation: Data 360 Data Shares (zero-copy data sharing) allow Data 360 objects to be securely shared with external platforms like Google BigQuery. This provides direct, read-only access without data movement, ETL pipelines, or data duplication, enabling low-latency analytics on unified customer data. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Scheduled batch exports introduce latency (minutes to hours) and create data duplication, violating the no‑duplication and minimal latency requirements. C: REST API endpoints are not designed for bulk analytics queries and may have rate limits and pagination overhead, making them unsuitable for large‑scale analytics. D: Custom ODBC connectors would require complex setup and ongoing maintenance; Data Shares provide a native, zero‑copy solution.

question: A sales operations manager wants account executives to see a timeline of a lead's recent webinar attendance and whitepaper downloads directly on the Lead record page in Salesforce. These activities are stored as "Interaction_DMO" records in Data 360. What is the most efficient way to display this timeline without custom development

options.A: Drag the Data 360 External Related List component onto the Lead Lightning page and configure it for Interaction_DMO
options.B: Build a Flow to sync Interaction_DMO records to a custom object and add a standard related list
options.C: Create a report chart filtered by Lead ID and embed it on the record page
options.D: Use Apex to query Data 360 APIs and render results in a custom Visualforce component

explanation: Data 360 External Related List (Related List Enrichment) is a native Lightning component that displays related external records from Data 360 DMOs directly on a Salesforce record page. The consultant can drag this component onto the Lead Lightning page and configure it to show Interaction_DMO records, requiring no custom code or data synchronization. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Syncing to a custom object creates data duplication, introduces latency, and requires ongoing maintenance, violating the “most efficient” requirement. C: Embedded report charts can query Data 360 but may have performance limitations and require report creation for each use case, and are not a native related list. D: Apex with custom Visualforce adds significant development effort and maintenance overhead when a native component exists.

question: A consultant has configured identity resolution rules to merge customer records from three source systems. Before deploying to production, they need to confirm that the rules are correctly merging expected records. Which two tools should the consultant use to validate the unified profile results

options.A: Profile Viewer and SQL Query Interface
options.B: Data Stream Dashboard and Activation Logs
options.C: Segment Builder and Calculated Insight Tester
options.D: Match Rule Simulator and Reconciliation Preview

explanation: Profile Viewer (Profile Explorer) allows consultants to search for and inspect unified profiles, showing which source records were merged and what attribute values were reconciled. SQL Query Interface (Query Editor/Data Explorer) enables running queries against DMOs to programmatically verify that identity resolution results are correctly stored and accessible. Together, they provide both visual and programmatic validation. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Data Stream Dashboard shows ingestion health, not identity resolution results. Activation Logs show audience delivery status, not unification details.

question: A data analyst creates a new workspace in Data Explorer but selects the "Marketing" data space because they were uncertain which data space to choose. When attempting to write a query, the "Customer_Transaction_DMO" is not available. The analyst knows this DMO exists in the "Sales" data space. What should the analyst do

options.A: Add the Sales data space to the existing Marketing workspace
options.B: Create a new workspace and select the Sales data space
options.C: Move the Customer_Transaction_DMO to the Marketing data space
options.D: Reference the DMO with a fully qualified name including the Sales data space prefix

explanation: A workspace in Data 360 is permanently tied to a single data space at creation time and cannot be changed. If the required DMO is in the Sales data space, the analyst must create a new workspace and select the Sales data space as the binding. The DMO will then be available for queries. Why the other options are incorrect: A: Data spaces cannot be added to an existing workspace after creation; the binding is immutable. C: DMOs cannot be moved between data spaces through workspace configuration; data spaces are defined in metadata and moving would require re‑ingesting.

question: A telecommunications company has a custom Salesforce object called "Alternate_Email__c" that stores secondary email addresses for contacts. The marketing team needs to use these email addresses for activation campaigns. To which Data 360 DMO should the consultant map this custom object

options.A: Contact Point Email DMO
options.B: Individual DMO
options.C: Contact DMO
options.D: Alternate_Email__c DMO

explanation: In Data 360's standard data model, email addresses should be mapped to the Contact Point Email DMO. This harmonizes email data from various sources (standard Contact email, custom Alternate_Email__c, etc.) into a common structure, enabling consistent segmentation, activation, and identity resolution based on email addresses. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Individual DMO represents a person's identity attributes but does not directly store email addresses; email is stored in Contact Point Email. C: Contact DMO stores contact attributes but email addresses belong in Contact Point Email for proper contact point management and standard activation. D: Keeping it as a custom DMO would not harmonize the data with standard email attributes, limiting functionality and requiring custom logic for activation.

question: A financial institution is preparing to build a loan approval prediction model using Einstein Studio with customer data from Data 360. Which essential step helps ensure the model produces fair and unbiased outcomes across different demographic groups

options.A: Reviewing the training dataset to identify and address demographic segments that are underrepresented
options.B: Disabling all calculated insights to prevent model overfitting
options.C: Ensuring the training dataset contains at least 50 million transaction records
options.D: Using only structured numeric data and excluding text fields from the training set

explanation: Auditing training data for underrepresented segments is essential to prevent algorithmic bias. If certain demographic or behavioral segments are underrepresented, the model may perform poorly or unfairly on those groups. Identifying and addressing these gaps through data augmentation or reweighting is a key ethical AI practice. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Disabling calculated insights does not relate to bias prevention; calculated insights are derived metrics, not a source of bias. C: Dataset size does not guarantee ethical outcomes; a large dataset can still be biased.

question: A consultant configures identity resolution match rules for a customer database where many records have missing email addresses. The consultant wants to ensure that a missing email address in one record does not prevent it from matching with another record that has a valid email. Which setting should the consultant enable

options.A: Skip empty field evaluation in match conditions
options.B: Exclude null records from identity processing
options.C: Default empty values to a placeholder string
options.D: Require all match fields to be populated before processing

explanation: The "Ignore Empty Value" option (skip empty field evaluation) determines whether empty (null or blank) fields are considered when evaluating a match condition. When enabled, empty values are ignored, meaning the rule does not require a match on that field if it is empty in either record. This prevents false mismatches due to missing data. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Excluding null records would lose valuable data; the goal is to include records while handling missing values intelligently, not discard them. C: Defaulting to placeholders would create false matches (e.g., all missing emails become "UNKNOWN"), leading to incorrect merges.

question: A data architect configures query federation to access a large dataset stored in Amazon Redshift. When a SQL query is executed from Data 360 against this federated source, where does the actual query execution occur

options.A: The query is pushed down to Redshift's compute layer, and only results are returned to Data 360
options.B: Data 360 downloads the entire Redshift table to its local storage before executing the query
options.C: The query executes in Data 360's internal compute engine after converting Redshift data to Parquet
options.D: Redshift exports the data to CSV, which Data 360 then queries locally

explanation: Query federation pushes SQL queries down to the external system's compute layer (pushdown optimization). The external system (Redshift) executes the query using its own compute resources, and only the result set is returned to Data 360. This minimizes data movement and leverages the external system's processing power. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Data 360 does not download entire tables; this would defeat the purpose of federation and cause data duplication and high network costs. C: Data 360 does not execute federated queries with its own engine; it delegates execution to the external system for pushdown.

question: A consultant needs to configure zero-copy query federation to read customer data from an external Amazon Redshift database. After gathering the Redshift hostname, database name, and service account credentials, what is the first action the consultant must take in Data 360

options.A: Register the Redshift instance as a federated source by creating a connection with the provided credentials
options.B: Create a data stream using the Bulk API with Redshift as the source type
options.C: Map the external Redshift tables directly to the Unified Individual DMO
options.D: Run a test query to validate that Redshift is accessible from Data 360

explanation: The first step in setting up zero-copy data federation is to establish a connection in Data 360 Setup using the provider's (Redshift) credentials. This defines the connection parameters (hostname, database, authentication). Only after the connection is established can the consultant configure data streams or run federated queries. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Bulk API is for traditional data ingestion, not for zero-copy federation setup; federation uses a different configuration path. C: Mapping external tables to DMOs comes after the connection and data stream are created; you cannot map before connection exists.

question: A retail company receives daily inventory files in a Google Cloud Storage bucket. A calculated insight computes "Low Stock Alert" based on unified product data, and a segment uses this insight for out-of-stock notifications. To ensure the most recent inventory data is reflected in the segment, what is the correct execution order

options.A: Ingest inventory files → Run product identity resolution → Refresh low stock calculated insight
options.B: Refresh low stock calculated insight → Ingest inventory files → Run product identity resolution
options.C: Run product identity resolution → Refresh low stock calculated insight → Ingest inventory files
options.D: Ingest inventory files → Refresh low stock calculated insight → Run product identity resolution

explanation: The correct sequence is: (1) Ingest inventory files (Refresh Data Stream) to bring new data into Data 360; (2) Run product identity resolution to match and unify product records across sources; (3) Refresh the calculated insight (Low Stock Alert) to recompute aggregates based on the updated unified data. This ensures segments using the insight reflect the latest inventory. Why the other options are incorrect: B: The calculated insight cannot refresh before data is ingested; it would compute stale results. C: Identity resolution cannot run before data is ingested; no new data to resolve. D: The calculated insight should run after identity resolution, not before, to ensure the unified view is used for aggregation.

question: A Data 360 Consultant is explaining sandbox behavior to a stakeholder. The stakeholder asks what happens to Data 360 configurations and data when a sandbox is refreshed from production. What is copied during a standard sandbox refresh

options.A: DMO definitions, data stream mappings, identity resolution rulesets, and calculated insight configurations
options.B: Complete copies of all production data lake objects and data model objects
options.C: A sample of 5,000 random customer records from each production DMO
options.D: Real-time query access to production data without any local storage

explanation: When a sandbox is refreshed, only metadata is copied from production, including DMO definitions, data stream configurations, identity resolution rulesets, calculated insights, segment definitions, and activation configurations. Source data (the actual customer records) is not copied; the sandbox does not contain production data. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Production data is not copied to sandboxes for security, privacy, and storage reasons. C: Data sampling is not a standard feature of sandbox refreshes; sandboxes are metadata-only unless explicitly configured otherwise. D: Sandboxes do not have real-time query access to production data lakes; they operate as isolated environments without production data.

question: A segment built on the "Customer_DMO" identifies high-value shoppers. The marketing team needs to include "Membership_Tier" from a separate "Loyalty_DMO" in the activation payload to personalize messaging, but the segment filters did not use this DMO. How can the consultant include this field without modifying the segment definition

options.A: During activation setup, add the Loyalty_DMO and select Membership_Tier as an additional field using Activation Membership
options.B: Create a calculated insight that joins Membership_Tier to Customer_DMO and rebuild the segment
options.C: Modify the data stream mapping to add Membership_Tier as a field on Customer_DMO
options.D: Add a contact point priority rule that copies Membership_Tier to the activation output

explanation: During activation setup, the consultant can use Activation Membership to include fields from related DMOs that were not used in the segment filters. By selecting the Loyalty_DMO and its Membership_Tier attribute, the exported payload will include those fields for each segment member without modifying the underlying segment definition. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Adding a calculated insight and rebuilding the segment adds unnecessary complexity and maintenance overhead, and changes the segment definition. C: Data stream mappings define ingestion, not activation output; modifying them would affect all downstream uses and is not scoped to this activation. D: Contact point priority rules are for identity resolution, not for including fields in activation payloads.

question: A Data 360 Consultant is building a model in Einstein Studio to predict the "Estimated Repair Cost" for warranty claims, which is a dollar amount (e.g., $47.50, $312.00, $1,250.00). Based on the target variable's data type, which model type is appropriate

options.A: Regression, because the target is a continuous numeric value
options.B: Binary Classification, because the outcome can be categorized as "high cost" vs "low cost"
options.C: Multiclass Classification, because dollar amounts can be bucketed into ranges
options.D: Clustering, because repair costs naturally form groups

explanation: Estimated Repair Cost is a continuous numeric value (dollar amount). Regression models are designed to predict continuous numerical outcomes, making them the correct choice. Classification models predict discrete categories and would lose precision. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Binary classification reduces a continuous measure to two arbitrary categories, losing precision and requiring subjective threshold definition. C: Bucketing into ranges changes the problem from regression to classification, but regression is more appropriate when the exact numeric value is valuable for cost estimation.

question: A subscription box service wants to send a personalized follow-up survey for every product shipment. If a customer receives three separate shipments, the audience should contain three distinct entries for that customer. Shipments are stored in the "Shipment_Order_DMO," and identity resolution unifies customers on "Unified_Customer_DMO." Which configuration produces one audience entry per shipment

options.A: Build the segment directly on the Shipment_Order_DMO
options.B: Build the segment on the Unified_Customer_DMO with a calculated insight
options.C: Build the segment on the Individual DMO with a filter on shipment count
options.D: Build the segment on a calculated insight that aggregates shipments by customer

explanation: To create one audience entry per shipment, the segment must be built on the Shipment_Order_DMO (the transaction object). Each Shipment_Order record becomes a distinct member in the segment. If segmented on Unified_Customer_DMO, each customer would appear only once regardless of shipment count. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Segmenting on Unified_Customer_DMO groups all shipments under one profile, producing one entry per customer, not per shipment. C: Individual DMO similarly groups shipments; it would not produce per-shipment entries.

question: A Data 360 Consultant reviews identity resolution metrics after a daily batch run. The source system contains 500,000 customer records, but only 12,000 profiles were processed. All runs completed successfully with no errors. What is the most likely reason for the low processed count

options.A: Only profiles with detected data changes since the last run were submitted for processing
options.B: The identity resolution match confidence threshold was set too high, excluding most profiles
options.C: The data stream frequency is configured to run at minimum frequency, limiting profile volume
options.D: A data quality filter excluded profiles with incomplete address fields

explanation: Identity Resolution uses incremental processing: only source profiles that have changed since the last processing run are submitted for unification. Unchanged profiles are skipped to optimize compute resources. After the initial full run, subsequent batches typically process only a small percentage of changed records, explaining why 12,000 out of 500,000 were processed. Why the other options are incorrect: B: Match confidence thresholds determine if profiles are merged, not whether they are processed at all. All profiles are processed regardless of confidence.

question: A logistics company detects package damage events from IoT sensors on delivery trucks. When a damage event occurs, an immediate warehouse inspection workflow must be triggered in Salesforce CRM with minimal delay. Which Data 360 capability should the architect use

options.A: A calculated insight refreshed every 30 seconds that evaluates damage event patterns
options.B: A manual activation triggered by a warehouse supervisor who monitors the event stream
options.C: A real-time data action configured to fire an event-triggered Salesforce Flow upon event ingestion
options.D: A scheduled batch transform running every 60 seconds to check for new damage events

explanation: Real-time data actions via automation event-triggered Flow provide the lowest latency for triggering a workflow in Salesforce CRM immediately upon event ingestion. The streaming event (package damage detection) triggers an automation directly, enabling sub-second reaction times for critical warehouse inspection workflows. Why the other options are incorrect: A: A calculated insight refreshed every 30 seconds still introduces latency (up to 30 seconds) and is not designed for sub-second event triggering. B: Manual activation requires human intervention, which is neither immediate nor automated, and introduces delays. D: A scheduled batch transform running every 60 seconds introduces up to 60 seconds of latency, failing the "immediate" requirement.

question: A consultant creates a calculated insight called "Customer_Profitability_Score" that appears as an option when building segments on the "Individual" DMO. However, the same insight does not appear when segmenting on the "Unified_Individual" DMO. What is the most likely cause

options.A: The consultant lacks "View" permissions on the Unified_Individual DMO
options.B: The calculated insight lacks a direct relationship path to the Unified_Individual DMO
options.C: The data space containing the calculated insight is different from the Unified_Individual data space
options.D: Calculated insights cannot be used for segmentation on unified profiles

explanation: For a calculated insight to be available when segmenting on Unified_Individual, the calculated insight must have a defined relationship path to the Unified_Individual DMO. If it only relates to Individual DMO (the source profile), it will appear only when segmenting on Individual, not Unified_Individual. Why the other options are incorrect: A: Permission issues would block access entirely, not make the insight appear for one DMO but not another. C: Data spaces do not affect visibility of calculated insights in segmentation in this manner; the issue is missing relationship. D: Calculated insights can be used for segmentation on unified profiles; the consultant must ensure the relationship is correctly configured.

question: During a data mapping exercise for an insurance client, a consultant finds that the standard "Policy_DMO" lacks fields for "Underwriting_Notes" and "Risk_Assessment_Score" — both critical for the claims team. Following best practices, what should the consultant do

options.A: Create two new custom DMOs, one for each missing field, and relate them to Policy_DMO
options.B: Ignore these fields since they are not part of the standard data model
options.C: Store these fields in a separate JSON blob within an existing DMO field
options.D: Add custom fields to the standard Policy_DMO to store Underwriting_Notes and Risk_Assessment_Score

explanation: Best practice is to extend the relevant standard DMO (Policy_DMO) by adding custom fields to accommodate business-specific attributes. This preserves relationship context, maintains standard functionality (calculated insights, segments, activations), and avoids fragmenting the data model. Why the other options are incorrect: A: Creating separate custom DMOs per field fragments the data model, complicates queries, and loses relationship context. B: Ignoring critical business fields fails to meet the client's requirements and defeats the purpose of the implementation. C: Storing fields in a JSON blob within an existing field makes the data difficult to query and index, and is not a best practice.

question: A telecommunications provider ingests customer account data from a legacy system. Each record contains both "Home_Phone_Plan_Data" and "Mobile_Phone_Plan_Data" in separate fields within the same record. The billing team needs to process each phone plan as an independent record. What should the consultant recommend

options.A: Ask the source system owner to modify the legacy system to split the records before export
options.B: Clone the source data object and manually delete irrelevant fields from each clone
options.C: Configure a batch transform that reads each source record and writes two separate output records
options.D: Create two separate data streams, one for home phone data and one for mobile phone data

explanation: A batch transform can take a single input record (with both home and mobile phone plan data) and output two separate records (one for each plan type) into a target DLO. This splits the data without modifying the source system, enabling independent tracking and processing. Why the other options are incorrect: A: Modifying the source system adds unnecessary complexity and may be outside the project scope; Data 360 can handle the split natively. B: Manual cloning and deletion is inefficient, error-prone, and not scalable for large datasets. D: Creating separate data streams does not solve the problem; the source data still arrives as single records containing both plan types, so each stream would still get the combined record.

question: A manufacturing company wants to track "Average Production Downtime" across factories, using data from ERP, IoT sensors, and Service Cloud. Different teams need to view this metric by factory location, machine type, and shift. The solution must provide near-real-time updates. Which Data 360 feature meets this requirement

options.A: A Salesforce report that queries Service Cloud data only
options.B: A formula field on the IoT sensor DMO that computes per-record downtime
options.C: A static dashboard exported from the ERP system monthly
options.D: A calculated insight that aggregates downtime events and can be refreshed on a schedule

explanation: A calculated insight can aggregate data from multiple sources (ERP, IoT sensors, Service Cloud) to compute Average Production Downtime. It can be refreshed near-real-time (on a configurable schedule) and supports multi-dimensional grouping, allowing teams to view the metric by factory location, machine type, or shift. Why the other options are incorrect: A: A Salesforce report limited to Service Cloud data would miss ERP and IoT sensor data, providing an incomplete picture. B: Formula fields perform row-level calculations, not aggregations like averages across many records from multiple sources. C: A monthly static dashboard does not provide near-real-time updates and would be stale, failing the requirement.

question: A media streaming company has deployed a "Churn Risk" prediction model using Einstein Studio. The retention team wants to automatically add high-risk customers to a priority outreach segment within minutes of the model scoring. How should predictions be applied to this business process

options.A: Use Identity Resolution to merge predictions into existing customer profiles without automation
options.B: Export prediction scores to CSV and have the retention team import them weekly
options.C: Schedule a predict job that writes risk scores to Data 360 DMOs, then use Flow Builder to add high-risk customers to the segment
options.D: Embed the Einstein Studio model URL in a Service Cloud Lightning page for manual review

explanation: The standard method is to use Einstein Studio's predict jobs (scheduled or on-demand) to write prediction scores to Data 360 DMOs, then use Flow Builder (or segment logic referencing the scores) to automatically add high-risk customers to the priority outreach segment. This integrates predictions directly into automated business processes. Why the other options are incorrect: A: Identity Resolution merges profiles but does not apply predictions or trigger automated segmentation; it is a separate process. B: Manual CSV export/import is not scalable, introduces latency, and requires manual intervention each cycle, violating the “within minutes” requirement. D: Embedding a URL provides UI access but does not automatically apply predictions to business processes; it requires human action.

question: A direct-to-consumer brand collects customer information from its website, mobile app, call center, and physical retail stores. Each channel stores data differently, leading to fragmented customer views and inconsistent messaging. What is Data 360's primary purpose in addressing this challenge

options.A: To generate automated email marketing campaigns based on browsing behavior
options.B: To replace all existing source systems with a single unified database
options.C: To unify and harmonize data from all channels into a single, complete customer profile
options.D: To archive historical customer data for long-term storage cost reduction

explanation: Data 360's primary purpose is to unify and harmonize data from multiple disparate sources (website, mobile app, call center, retail stores) into a single, complete customer profile. This unified view enables consistent personalization, analytics, segmentation, and activation across all customer touchpoints. Why the other options are incorrect: A: Email campaign automation is an application built on top of unified data, not the core purpose of Data 360. B: Data 360 does not replace source systems; it ingests and unifies data from them while they continue to operate. D: Data archiving for cost reduction is a potential benefit but not the primary purpose of Data 360.

question: A global financial institution has three divisions: Retail Banking, Wealth Management, and Commercial Lending. All divisions must use the same Data 360 home org but keep their customer data, DMOs, and segments fully separated for regulatory compliance. Which mechanism provides this logical isolation

options.A: Assign different permission sets to users from each division within a single data space
options.B: Create a separate data space for each division within the same home org
options.C: Use record-type filtering on all DMOs to restrict access based on division
options.D: Build separate companion connections for each division pointing to different source systems

explanation: Data spaces in Data 360 provide logical separation of data and metadata within a single home org. question: A healthcare organization is ingesting patient vitals data from wearable devices. question: A marketing analyst creates a Salesforce report based on a calculated insight that shows "Daily Active Users." The analyst notices that the report does not reflect user activity from the last hour. What is the critical limitation the consultant should have communicated
